RC6 moves context retrieval into the normal submitted-prompt path. The supported Codex hook
uses the actual prompt and provides required guidance and selected source references before
task-specific reads. It keeps the coding model fixed. Native host trust and project-owned hook
customizations still require deliberate setup.
When a Codex session resumes under a new process, prompt context can continue after proving the
old process absent and the pinned runtime current; the prior startup reader keeps its separate
cleanup obligation.

- A disposable SQLite source index belongs to each worktree. It keeps bounded source facts,
  ranges, literal descriptions and resolved declared links. Unchanged facts can be reused; changed
  source is rechecked before delivery. `context-index status` is passive; `refresh` and `--rebuild`
  explicitly reconcile the current worktree. The shared continuity task/history store stays
  separate, at schema 6.
- Optional JEV selection traverses the full metadata-approved inventory in bounded batches,
  independent of an initial keyword shortlist. An entry can request two expansions that share
  its call and byte allowance. Packets distinguish assessed, unanswered, unavailable and
  outside-permission paths. Missing credentials, model uncertainty, exhaustion and provider errors
  retain local context and access to original files. Hosted metadata and source permissions remain
  separate; existing profiles do not gain permission through an upgrade.
- Current-source overviews also feed the existing documentation checks and advisory backfill
  observations. No generated description corpus, shared cross-worktree index or automatic model
  delegation is added. Structural extraction is strongest for TS/JS and Markdown; other languages
  may have only literal clues. A partial index or incomplete JEV coverage is never a no-match proof.
- Entry, selection, expansion, task binding and outcome receipts make ordinary usage measurable.
  Native task qualification and controlled JEV calls prove the integration path, not time or token
  savings. Host coverage outside the qualified Codex path, adopter outcomes and physical-device
  behavior remain unproved by this context-focused release.

Adoption is deliberate. Follow the [RC6 setup guide](../../docs/guides/rc6-prompt-context.md) to
reconcile the managed hook, trust its exact definition, review metadata/source roots and confirm
the fixed model and no-token fallback. The tracked Codex hook now resolves the current worktree;
its local launcher and receipt store remain separate. An RC5 absolute-path startup hook requires
the guide's deliberate clean cutover; an in-place update will not silently retain it. Update a
linked worktree at a safe seam after its tracked
pin arrives through Git; an open merge blocks automatic startup adoption. The
[worktree guide](../../docs/developer/guides/source-control-and-worktrees.md) describes the
supported reconciliation flow. Finish RC5 jobs and reconcile linked worktrees before resuming
shared-history writes on RC6. Mixed-version writing is outside this release qualification.
